site.title: Antidote — interpretable adaptive audio research
site.description: A transparent research program for translating semantic intent into inspectable generative-audio journeys and carefully separated response evidence.

hero.title: Shape a journey without hiding the decisions.
hero.description: Antidote is a local-first research program for expressing a desired transition, reviewing a semantic journey, generating bounded audio, and keeping intended controls, realized acoustics, exposure, and personal response separate.

demo.title: The instrument is transparent; the scientific claims remain bounded.
demo.description: The repository contains an executable synthetic desktop session and deterministic mock worker. A real model, formal participant study, and therapeutic-efficacy evidence are not yet available.

features.title: Keep meaning, generation, listening, and response inspectable.
features.description: Each boundary has an explicit owner and produces evidence for the next human decision.

items.title: Describe the desired journey
items.description: Capture the present moment, direction, inclusions, exclusions, duration, and uncertainty in language a person can inspect and edit.

items.title: Review before generation
items.description: Expose the semantic stages, acoustic controls, rationales, unsupported capabilities, and immutable generation specification before approval.

items.title: Verify what was produced
items.description: Record worker identity, parameters, warnings, realized features, artifact hashes, and provenance without treating generation as a successful response.

items.title: Let the person interpret the experience
items.description: Keep actual exposure, felt response, mismatch, harm, usefulness, and optional later aftereffect distinct from system intent.

useCases.title: One framework, several deliberately separated questions.
useCases.description: Technical controllability, experiential feasibility, efficacy, and mechanism require different evidence and cannot substitute for one another.

items.title: System design
items.description: Formalize a person–moment–journey model, semantic intent mixer, predictive horizon, and continuity constraints as testable design proposals.

items.title: Technical verification
items.description: Test contract fidelity, control adherence, latency, buffering, deterministic fixtures, provenance, and failure behavior.

items.title: Later feasibility research
items.description: Evaluate within-person experience only through a frozen protocol with consent, stopping rules, null outcomes, harms, and uncertainty.

faq.title: What the current work does—and does not—establish.
faq.description: Clear status language is part of the system, not a disclaimer added afterward.

items.question: Is Antidote a treatment?
items.answer: No. It is a research and reflective-wellness prototype. The paper does not establish clinical efficacy, diagnosis, or a neurological mechanism.

items.question: Does the current MVP use a real generative model?
items.answer: No. The executable path uses a deterministic synthetic mock worker. A real adapter requires a separate license, integrity, hardware, safety, and control-adherence review.

items.question: Does Holon own Antidote's content or identity?
items.answer: No. Holon owns reusable materialization and rendering profiles. Antidote owns its reviewed content, visual inputs, research claims, paper artifacts, and publication decisions.

items.question: Has a participant study started?
items.answer: No. The design/protocol manuscript can define a future method, but merging it does not authorize collection or imply ethics approval.

documentation.introduction: Use Antidote by preserving consent, human authority, evidence class, provenance, and the distinction between intended controls and observed response.

pages.title: Start with Antidote
pages.summary: Orient to the research, publication, and synthetic prototype boundaries.
pages.body:
Antidote combines a reproducible research workspace with an emerging local research instrument. Begin with the [paper](/paper/) for the design and evidence boundary, then use the architecture surface to inspect responsibility and trust zones. The current executable session uses synthetic fixtures and a deterministic mock worker; no real model or participant result is implied.

The repository-owned Make and Task commands build the paper independently. The public site adds Holon's exact-pinned presentation profiles without changing manuscript source, paper bytes, publication provenance, or Antidote's authority over claims.

pages.title: Publication and integrity
pages.summary: Verify the paper, site composition, exact revision, and complete checksum inventory.
pages.body:
The [publication manifest](/publication.json) describes the paper artifacts. The [site catalog](/site.json) describes stable routes and honest publication slots. The [site-suite evidence](/site-suite.provenance.json) records Holon's immutable commit and blueprint identities. [SHA256SUMS](/SHA256SUMS) covers every staged public file.

The paper remains available as accessible HTML, PDF, provenance JSON, and an independently compilable arXiv source archive. The magazine route remains planned with no fabricated edition or download.

pages.title: Prototype boundary
pages.summary: Understand what the executable synthetic session proves.
pages.body:
The Rust core owns consent, session transitions, journey approval, orchestration, events, safety policy, and provenance. React and Tauri own presentation and desktop capability. The isolated Python worker receives only an approved semantic projection, accepted journey plan, and immutable generation specification.

The deterministic mock proves protocol behavior and failure handling. It does not establish model quality, experiential benefit, clinical efficacy, or mechanism. Real-model selection and formal data collection require later evidence and review gates.

pages.title: Contributing
pages.summary: Keep proposed behavior and scientific claims proportional to checked-in evidence.
pages.body:
Before changing claims, methods, results, or conclusions, read the epistemology, scientific boundaries, claim ledger, and relevant primary-source records. Before changing runtime behavior, read the system, architecture, accepted decisions, and affected contracts.

Use `make check-all` or `task check-all` for the paper and `make check-site HOLON_SOURCE=../holon` or its Task equivalent for the exact-pinned public composition. Never place private health, therapy, journal, credential, participant, or model-token data in fixtures or public source.

architecture.title: Antidote architecture
architecture.introduction: Antidote separates research truth, human authority, local runtime behavior, replaceable model execution, and public projections.
architecture.diagram:
flowchart TD
  person[Person and present moment] --> consent[Consent-scoped projection]
  consent --> core[Rust domain and application core]
  core --> plan[Inspectable journey plan]
  plan --> worker[Capability-scoped model worker]
  worker --> artifact[Audio artifact and feature report]
  artifact --> exposure[Deliberate exposure and stop]
  exposure --> response[Person-reported response]
  response --> core
  core --> export[Privacy-reviewed provenance export]

legal.introduction: Public policy projections identify their evidence and update boundary; they do not replace the canonical repository records.

pages.title: Licensing
pages.summary: Separate repository, manuscript, figure, framework, dependency, model, and generated-audio rights.
pages.body:
The repository publishes its applicable license in canonical source. The manuscript, figures, third-party references, Holon profiles, Zensical dependency graph, future model assets, and generated audio may have different terms. Review the corresponding source records and notices before reuse.

The public site does not grant rights to future model weights, training data, participant material, private records, or generated audio merely by linking to the research program.

pages.title: Accessibility
pages.summary: Static readability, keyboard access, focus, contrast, reduced motion, and artifact accessibility are release concerns.
pages.body:
The publication checks semantic landmarks, headings, local links, focus behavior, responsive layouts, reduced motion, PDF properties, and accessible web output. Automated checks support but do not replace human review.

Report barriers through the Antidote issue tracker with the route, browser, assistive technology, and reproduction steps. The paper remains available in both accessible HTML and PDF projections.

pages.title: Scientific and safety boundary
pages.summary: A transparent prototype and intense experience do not establish benefit, treatment, or mechanism.
pages.body:
Antidote is a research and reflective-wellness prototype, not a medical treatment or diagnostic system. The originating N-of-1 experience is hypothesis-generating context only. Intended controls, generated acoustics, actual exposure, felt response, usefulness, harm, and later aftereffect remain distinct.

Formal participant collection requires a frozen protocol, consent and privacy review, stopping rules, adverse-event handling, and appropriate independent review. Merging code or a protocol does not authorize collection.

pages.title: Privacy and local-first limits
pages.summary: Local-first narrows exposure but is not a claim of perfect security or secure deletion.
pages.body:
The target instrument keeps canonical state and generation local and sends the worker only an approved semantic projection. Private journal, therapy, health, participant, credential, and model-token data must not enter this repository, public fixtures, logs, or publication artifacts.

Encryption, key recovery, backup, retention, deletion, crash reporting, and operating-system isolation require explicit implementation and review before non-developer personal use. Provenance does not prove truth, consent, ownership, or clinical validity.
